questions.stem: Two angles on a straight line are (3x + 10) degrees and (2x + 20) degrees. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line sum to 180 degrees. So (3x + 10) + (2x + 20) = 180. This gives 5x + 30 = 180, so 5x = 150, and x = 30.

questions.stem: Three angles meet at a point. Two of the angles are 127 degrees and 95 degrees. What is the third angle?
questions.explanation: Angles at a point sum to 360 degrees. The third angle = 360 - 127 - 95 = 138 degrees.

questions.stem: Two straight lines cross. One of the angles formed is 72 degrees. What is the angle directly opposite it?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal. The angle directly opposite 72 degrees is also 72 degrees.

questions.stem: Angles on a straight line are x degrees, 2x degrees, and 60 degrees. Find the value of x.
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line sum to 180 degrees. So x + 2x + 60 = 180. This gives 3x = 120, so x = 40.

questions.stem: Two straight lines cross. The four angles formed are a, b, a, and b. If a = (4x - 10) degrees and b = (2x + 40) degrees, find the value of a.
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles on a straight line sum to 180 degrees: a + b = 180. So (4x - 10) + (2x + 40) = 180, giving 6x + 30 = 180, so 6x = 150 and x = 25. Therefore a = 4(25) - 10 = 100 degrees.
